name: Dysarthria following other nontraumatic intracranial hemorrhage
description: Dysarthria is a speech sound disorder resulting from neurological injury of the motor component of the motor–speech system and is characterized by poor articulation of phonemes. Those affected lack sufficient control of the muscles used for speech to pronounce words clearly.

red_flags.condition: [LLM DRAFT] Sudden or progressive loss of motor function indicating possible extension of intracranial hemorrhage or secondary brain injury.
[LLM DRAFT] New-onset or recurrent seizure activity signaling acute neurological deterioration in the setting of nontraumatic intracranial hemorrhage.
